title: Rules made from words are saved but the Mac's host never checks them
body:
Shakeout on the owner Mac (host: ~/.openagents/dev-host/current → 32a6df832d, started Oct 2 17:08; CLI at eeae76ff5a):
```
openagents background draft --id shake900 -- "notify me when free disk space is under 900 GB"   # dry run: "would tell you: Disk space is low: 502 GB free"
openagents background apply shake900   # "Saved … It runs on its own from now on"
# 9+ minutes later (interval 5 min):
openagents background log low-disk-900gb   # No runs yet.
```
`~/.openagents/background/state.json` has entries only for `disk` and `disk-cleanup`; `disk-cleanup` is checked every 5 min, the new rule (in `background/rules/low-disk-900gb.json`) never is. So either the running host does not load rules added after it started, or that host build predates rules from words — either way the CLI tells the user it runs when it does not. Expected: the host picks up saved rules without a restart (or `apply` signals it), and if the running host can’t run a rule, `apply`/`list` say so. Also the Mac dev host is ~8h behind main; CoderOS self-updates when idle, this Mac doesn’t seem to. Minor: there is no `background remove ID`; removal only works by words (`draft "remove the rule X"` + `apply`). (Test rules removed afterwards.)
